reasoning: Base-rates lane. (1) Price base rate: LEU's annual log returns 2021-26 have sd ~1.0 (Oct-to-Oct: -13%, +19%, +51%, +149%, -125%) and realised vol is 89%; for such a stock an efficient-market forecast has a median ~20-25% below spot (E[P] ~ spot x 1.10 with sd 0.75), so P(up) is ~0.40 before any view. (2) Positioning: 30% of float short (StockAnalysis); Asquith-Pathak-Ritter find high-short-interest stocks underperform mainly when shorting is constrained (equal-weighted -215bp/month), a mild negative; a -71% year is a momentum loser, but LEU's own history shows violent rebounds (2022 low $21 -> $33 by Dec; April 2025 $54 -> $400 by Oct 2025). (3) Events: Kalshi/Polymarket price a December Fed hike at ~76-77% (rate-sensitive nuclear basket fell with the 10-year at 5.26%); Polymarket gives a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire by Oct-31 only 1.6%, and the US ban ends Russian LEU imports on 2028-01-01 regardless, so Centrus' trading book (over half Russian-sourced to 2027) runs off. (4) Project base rates: of four US enrichment new-builds in 2004-12 only Urenco's reached operation; USEC's ACP at this very site was halted in 2009. Orano's brownfield extension costs EUR 680/SWU-yr; I assume ~2x for Centrus' first-of-a-kind ramp. With a $215 LEU / $480 HALEU SWU level, 50% margin (Urenco 38-46%), p 0.675 and DOE's $900M milestones, the initial build is worth -$0.38B risked from 2026-07-01 including spend already committed, so value rests on net cash, the run-off core and the expansion option: engine fair value $59 (bear $37, bull $87), well under the 19-analyst average target of $241. (5) Ladder: 80% weight on the efficient-market lognormal (median $93, sd 0.75) and 20% on my research distribution (median $59, sd 0.55): median ~$83, mean ~$112, P(>= $109.88) 0.355. The key judgment is capex per SWU; at Orano-level cost my value would be ~$95-100.

model_inputs.structure_note: Centrus is a fuel-cycle trading book (Russian TENEX + Orano SWU resold under contracts) funding a first-of-a-kind US centrifuge build-out. The engine's 3 years are the CORE book only (LEU trading + Technical Solutions + Westerman from Q4 2026), GAAP EBIT before build-out 'growth costs'; the core runs off after the Russian import ban closes on 2028-01-01, so FY2028 revenue falls 19% and the fixed DCF fades from there (a run-off, not a peak). All build-out spend from 2026-07-01 (capex + expensed growth costs) and its cash flows sit in one rNPV programme in 'adjustment' mode (initial ~1.5M SWU incl. 12 tU/yr HALEU) with DOE task-order milestones as milestones_pv. Value is carried by the DCF (0.40, engine) and two custom legs (market-share states 0.25; cash floor + real options 0.25); EV/EBITDA is a 0.10 cross-check (method_fit cap). Reverse DCF is shown as a 0-weight check.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian (each moves fair value >5%): (1) initial build-out spend $2.2B from 2026-07-01 (~$1,470/SWU-yr, ~2x Orano's EUR 680/SWU-yr brownfield extension); at Orano-level cost (~$1.2B) fair value rises by roughly $35-40/share; (2) SWU level price $215 LEU / $480 HALEU-SWU and 50% cash margin after maintenance (Urenco EBITDA margin 38-46% 2023-25); (3) success probability 0.675 for the initial build (US 2004-12 enrichment wave: 1 of 4 projects reached operation; Centrus' own HALEU demo cascade did deliver); (4) 40% chance of a further ~$400M equity raise before the horizon. Converts: 2.25% 2030 notes ($97.50 conversion) are in the money - principal in cash, net share settlement ~0.47M shares at $110 included; 0% 2032 notes ($229.62) out of the money; common warrants ($226.86-$362.98) out of the money and ignored. Defense adjacency: Antares/Radiant HALEU offtakes serve military microreactor programmes; estimated <3% of horizon-year revenue (no disclosed values) - flagged, not excluded. Engine DCF $44 vs other legs $69 (-36%): the DCF sees only the run-off core plus the risked build-out and none of the expansion option, which the custom legs carry.
